overview: Written for the beginning of Leviticus, this poem reflects on the tension of living freely in the Diaspora while family and fellow Jews endure hardship in Israel. Inspired by the question of how to fulfill our mission outside of Israel, the poet calls on Jews everywhere to take their place in the never-ending scroll — if our brothers and sisters take up the sword, we must take up the pen. Dedicated to our brothers and sisters in Israel, and Am Yisrael all over the world.
poem_lines: my family are stuck in exodus.
While I walk abroad as a free man,
my family shelter in the land.
While my soul is in the east
my body is in the west.
while I live in a palace,
As our people take a toll
So if they die for us
If they take up the sword,
We must take up the pen.
poem_hebrew_lines: בעוד אני הולך בחו״ל כאיש חופשי,
